userStories.name: Align Vertex scenario-run clients with mounted routes
userStories.description: When web helpers, SDKs, and cookbook snippets start or cancel a Vertex scenario run, use the mounted `/api/vertex/v1/scenarios/{scenarioRid}/runs` route family and the server's `runRid` accepted response instead of the stale singular `/run` client contract.
bdd_acceptance: Given the frontend scenario-run request builders receive a scenario RID, When they build start, stream, and cancel paths, Then the paths use `/runs` and encode the scenario/run IDs consistently with the server contract.

Given TypeScript, Python, and Go SDK clients start a scenario run, When their tests record the outgoing request, Then the request targets `/api/vertex/v1/scenarios/{scenarioRid}/runs` rather than the stale `/run` path.
Given the Vertex quickstart documents scenario execution, When readers follow the curl path, Then it matches the mounted `/runs` route family and no longer advertises the removed singular run route.

userStories.name: Expose Vertex scenario-run polling helpers
userStories.description: Add small SDK/web helpers that poll `GET /api/vertex/v1/scenarios/{scenarioRid}/runs/{runRid}` until terminal state so upper-layer clients can observe run completion before a dedicated SSE run stream is mounted.
bdd_acceptance: Given a run start returns `runRid` and `pending`, When a polling helper is invoked, Then it calls the documented GET run route until the run is terminal.
Given the run transitions to failed or canceled, When polling completes, Then the helper returns the terminal status and error/checkpoint details instead of assuming success.
Given polling exceeds a caller-supplied timeout or abort signal, When the helper exits, Then it reports a cancellation/timeout without leaking timers.

userStories.name: Gate stale Vertex scenario-run debug route
userStories.description: Audit the Vertex scenario debug drawer's `/api/vertex/v1/scenario-runs/{rid}/debug` fetch path against mounted server routes and either wire/document the route or replace it with the public scenario-run record endpoint.
bdd_acceptance: Given the debug drawer fetches a scenario run, When the server route table is inspected, Then the requested route is mounted and documented or the drawer uses the documented run record endpoint.
Given a run is missing, When the drawer fetch fails, Then the UI presents the typed not-found state without an unhandled promise rejection.
Given the route remains intentionally unavailable, When the contract test runs, Then it fails with a precise non-mounted-route decision rather than leaving an unreachable client path.
